stage_2_story.text_en:
On his last day in London, David decided to explore the famous Portobello Road marketplace. He had heard it was the best place to find souvenirs and local treasures, so he arrived early with his wallet full of British currency.

At the first stall, he spotted a set of hand-painted ceramic mugs. The seller wanted fifteen pounds each, but David smiled and offered ten. After a friendly back-and-forth, they agreed on eleven pounds — a real bargain! He made sure to ask for a receipt, just in case.

A little further down the street, he found a small boutique selling traditional English scarves. There was a large sign in the window: 'End of Season — forty percent discount on everything!' He could not resist. He bought two scarves and kept both receipts carefully in his coat pocket.

Before paying, David asked the shop assistant about the exchange rate between pounds and shekels. She was not sure, so he checked on his phone and decided the price was still very fair.

On the way back to the hotel, he passed through the airport and stopped at the duty-free shop to pick up whisky and chocolates as gifts. He smiled to himself — good souvenirs, great bargains, and no regrets.
